question: State the principle of a potentiometer. Explain why it is preferred over a voltmeter for measuring emf and calculate the emf of a cell if the potential gradient is $0.015\,\text{V cm}^{-1}$ and the balance length is $100\,\text{cm}$.

options.A: The potential drop is inversely proportional to wire length; a potentiometer draws maximum current from the cell; $\varepsilon=0.15\,\text{V}$.
options.B: The potential drop is independent of wire length; a potentiometer and voltmeter measure emf with equal accuracy; $\varepsilon=15\,\text{V}$.
options.C: For a uniform wire carrying steady current, $V\propto l$ or $V=kl$; at null balance a potentiometer draws no current from the cell, so it measures emf more accurately than a voltmeter; $\varepsilon=kl=(0.015)(100)=1.5\,\text{V}$.
options.D: For a uniform wire, $V\propto \dfrac{1}{l}$; a potentiometer measures terminal potential difference by drawing current; $\varepsilon=0.015\,\text{V}$.
